correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier transform c_n=a(1-(-1)^n exp(-pi a))/(pi(a^2+n^2)) is positive; the cosine factor shifts by one index, so Herglotz positivity reduces exactly to b>=-min_n 2c_n/(c_{n-1}+c_{n+1}). Algebra yields R_n=h^(+/-1)F_A(n) and excludes n=0. Differentiating F_A(sqrt y) gives one positive critical y=s_A^2 and strict unimodality, proving the <=4 parity candidates. At b=-B only finitely many modes vanish; all sufficiently large consecutive modes are strictly positive, and a Vandermonde argument makes every distinct-point Gram matrix positive definite. Taylor/scale estimates justify both asymptotics and the n-asymptotic; taking s_A=n yields a polynomially separated unique minimum dominating exponentially small parity splitting. Independent Sympy identities and 11-parameter/40-index checks support, not prove, the universal claims.

final_claim: For a>0, the geodesic-circle kernel K_{a,b}=exp(-a theta)(1+b cos theta) is positive definite iff b>=-B(a), where B is a minimum of at most four parity-dependent explicit Fourier ratios; all admissible kernels including the boundary are strictly positive definite on distinct point sets; B(a)~9 pi a/40 for a down to 0 and B(a)=1-9/(16 a^2)+O(a^-4) as a grows, and all sufficiently large indices arise uniquely as critical Fourier frequencies.
